clue.text: One concealed by secretive type? Right

indicators.note: something concealed by another is wrapped up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: someone tight-lipped is said to clam up, so a clam is a secretive person
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A question about who is hiding someone, answered with a brisk 'Right'.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim is an entitlement, something one has a right to.

clue.text: Dishonest player in club, say? Exactly!

parts.note: a club is one example of a playing card
sharp means exactly or precisely, as in 'six o'clock sharp'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cheat belongs in a club and is told 'Exactly!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a society, but it is a card suit, with 'say' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a professional cheat at card games.

clue.text: A pullover as present

parts.note: pull is draw, and over means turned the other way, giving draw read backwards

explanation.surface: A jumper is handed over as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pullover' looks like a jumper (a sweater) but splits as 'pull' (DRAW) and 'over', which turns it into WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize, something presented to someone.

clue.text: Attractiveness of publication, new version of Times

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication

indicators.note: a version of a word is a rearranged form of its letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper's appeal lies in a new edition of the Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges TIMES into ETISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetism is personal charm that draws people in.

clue.text: He's tucked into an African fowl

indicators.note: a piece tucked into another is slipped inside it, so one goes within the other

parts.note: a Guinean is a native of Guinea in West Africa
the word he, with 's as 'is' linking it to what follows

explanation.surface: A man has been stowed inside a bird from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African fowl' looks like one phrase, but 'African' belongs to the wordplay (GUINEAN) and only 'fowl' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The guinea hen is a speckled African game bird, a kind of domestic poultry.

clue.text: Big noise made by exploding grenade

indicators.note: an exploding word is blown apart into new letters

explanation.surface: A loud bang comes from a grenade going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big noise' sounds like a bang, but it means an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a person of high rank, a VIP or bigwig.

clue.text: After Eastern state, name a state in Midwest

parts.note: India is a country in the East

explanation.surface: Geography: after an Asian country, name a Midwestern US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the US states of the Midwest, next to Illinois.

clue.text: East wind disturbed the old king

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of their usual order

explanation.surface: An easterly gale troubled an ancient monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges WIND into DWIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin was a seventh-century king of Northumbria.

clue.text: Difficult point about one resolution

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the first pieces go round the next

parts.note: hard means difficult
a ness is a headland or point of land
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A tricky point concerns one resolution of a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: HARDNESS goes 'about' I. 'Resolution' looks like an answer to a problem but means resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardiness is toughness and endurance, the firmness of a resolute person.

clue.text: Do some jogging, without a stitch, around midnight

indicators.note: around means the first piece encircles the second

parts.note: someone without a stitch on is nude
the middle of the word night is the letter G

explanation.surface: A naked runner goes out jogging at midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogging' looks like running, but to jog someone is to push them lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge is to jog or prod someone gently.

clue.text: Hold up transport worker in van? Just the opposite

parts.note: to rear is to raise or lift up
a guard is the official in charge of a train

explanation.surface: A railway guard is being held up in a van.
explanation.walkthrough: The van, short for vanguard, is the front of an army; the definition asks for its opposite, the troops at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The rearguard protects the back of a marching force, where the vanguard leads at the front.

clue.text: Planet revolved rapidly, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is something said aloud, so the letters entered match a spoken word

parts.note: whirled means spun round fast

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a planet spun quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The world is our own planet, the Earth.

clue.text: Is pulling out one border plant

indicators.note: pulling out means one letter is removed from the word before it

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
an edge is a border or rim

explanation.surface: Someone is uprooting a plant from the garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulling out one' takes I from IS, leaving S; 'border plant' looks like a garden bed, but 'border' gives EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant of wet ground.

clue.text: Unusually dapper in one sort of trousers

indicators.note: letters arranged unusually are put in an unexpected order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone looks unusually smart in a particular style of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges DAPPER, IN and I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Drainpipes are very narrow-legged trousers, fashionable with 1950s Teddy boys.

clue.text: How stupid, as one bridge-player doubled opponent

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: doubled means the pair of pieces before it is written out twice

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
in bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so N stands for one of them
East is the bridge opponent of North, giving E

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark about a bridge player who doubled an opponent's bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubled' writes I and N (one bridge-player) twice: ININ. In bridge, a player 'doubles' an opponent's bid, which is the surface's misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means as foolish as a donkey, so it fits an exclamation at stupidity.

clue.text: Two rivers in delta confusedly mingle together

indicators.note: letters muddled confusedly are put in a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, twice

explanation.surface: Two rivers mix messily in a delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusedly' rearranges RR, IN and DELTA together.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlard is to intersperse or mix one thing through another.

clue.text: Skill required to make speech

definitions.meaning: a formal talk to an audience

explanation.definitionFit: Address means both deftness in handling things and a formal speech.

clue.text: Like plane taking pair to America after start of last month

parts.note: the first of December, written as Dec I
a duo is a pair
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: An aircraft takes two people to America in early December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' looks like an aircraft, but it is the plane tree, which sheds its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane tree loses its leaves each autumn, as a deciduous tree does.

clue.text: Succeeded with wit or use of a more tangible weapon

definitions.text: use of a more tangible weapon

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
wordplay is verbal wit

explanation.surface: Someone won with clever words rather than a real blade.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition contrasts the wit of WORDPLAY with the blade: fencing uses a weapon you can actually touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Swordplay is fencing, fighting with a real sword rather than verbal sparring.

clue.text: Get from one river to another, coming back for one more

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
taken as written

indicators.note: coming back means the last river named is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: Instructions for travelling from one river to another and back again.
explanation.walkthrough: From PO to CAM, with CAM coming back as MAC. 'Get from' and 'for' join the parts, and the definition says the answer is just one more river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac is another river, the one flowing past Washington DC.

clue.text: Cheerful person making an approach

definitions.meaning: in golf, an approach shot to the green is often a chip

explanation.definitionFit: Chipper means bright and cheerful, and also one who plays a golf chip shot.

clue.text: One accepted by Constable as likewise a great artist

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in, so it goes inside

parts.note: PC is police constable
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written
so means likewise, as in 'so am I'

explanation.surface: John Constable is said to accept someone else as a fellow great painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable looks like the English landscape painter, but it is a police constable, PC.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, among the greatest artists of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Progressive Christian, for example

parts.note: Christian is the hero of Bunyan's The ... Progress, the traveller on a religious journey

explanation.definitionFit: In Bunyan's allegory The Pilgrim's Progress, Christian is the traveller journeying to the Celestial City.

clue.text: A fabulous creature in vessel is confined to small area

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits within it

parts.note: a phial is a small glass bottle
taken as written
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A legendary beast is kept in a jar and so confined to a small space.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochial means limited to a parish, so narrow in outlook or scope.

clue.text: Artistic little boys set it up

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: An instruction to put something upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are the chubby infant cherubs of Renaissance painting.

clue.text: Pessimist, extremely crusty and not altogether pleasant

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
not altogether means the word falls just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A gloomy person who is very bad-tempered and not entirely likeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of CRUSTY, and 'not altogether' cuts NICE to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic expects the worst of people, much as a pessimist does.

clue.text: French artist's saintly patron

definitions.meaning: Jacques-Louis ... was the leading French Neoclassical painter
Saint ... is the patron saint of Wales

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a French painter and to the patron saint of Wales.

clue.text: Approve no medicine containing such poisonous stuff

indicators.note: the clue words contain the answer within them, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A warning not to sanction any drug made with toxic ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is the poison of snakes and stinging creatures.

clue.text: American humorist popular with Scottish company?

parts.note: two's company, and twa is Scots for two
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An American comic writer finds favour with a Scottish firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' looks like a business, but it is the saying 'two's company', read in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, author of Tom Sawyer, was America's best-known humorous writer.

clue.text: A boy given directions by head of Latin staff

parts.note: per means for each, a, as in fifty pence a head
a son is a boy
N and E are two compass directions

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A youngster is told the way by the senior Latin teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' becomes PER, the Latin 'for each' (so much a day = per day).
explanation.definitionFit: Personnel are the people employed by an organisation, its staff.

clue.text: Improper behaviour during code breaking? Odd

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: breaking scrambles the word it governs into new letters

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone finds bad behaviour while cracking a code strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges CODE into DECO.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a lack of propriety or good manners.

clue.text: Showing very little change? Yes, a minute variation

indicators.note: a variation of letters reorders them

explanation.surface: A question about slight change is answered with a minute variation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' rearranges YES, A and M (minute).
explanation.definitionFit: Samey is an informal word for monotonous, too alike throughout.
